newsitem.title: UK: Gas oil traders ponder fallout of Nov IPE play.
newsitem.headline: Gas oil traders ponder fallout of Nov IPE play.

text.p: European gas oil traders were split into bulls and bears on Wednesday about the implications of a record high physical delivery into the November IPE futures.

Differences centred on the viability of a play by the dominant long on the November contract, trading house Cargill, which dealers believe is due to take almost all of Tuesday's record 865,100 tonnes delivery.

Both Cargill and the dominant short in the market, Monte Carlo-based AIC, on Wednesday were pursuing a psychological duel to convince the market that they were comfortable with their respective positions.

Bulls argued that AIC would struggle to meet its large short position and Cargill would successfully ship its product into short positions in Europe and Asia. Bears countered that AIC had more than enough oil to meet its IPE sales and that the Rotterdam market would not be able to absorb it.
Bulls said Cargill could sell 500,000 tonnes into its network of downstream suppliers in inland Germany, 100,000 tonnes into France and 250,000 tonnes under arbitrage to Asia.
"Make your calculations and you will see it pays to go to Asia," one trader said.

Bears said Cargill would be able to place only 350,000 tonnes in Europe and Asia and would be forced to store around 500,000 tonnes for eventual sale in December. They questioned whether the arbitrage to Asia was open in any case.
"Does that sound like it will make money?" said one trader. "Find out some ship rates and see whether that makes sense to you that they take some to Asia."
Another bear trader said: "The market will be under tremendous pressure in the next few days. Basically the whole gas oil market will come down."
Cargill's net trading position was complicated by what traders said were probable earlier gains made on the Nov/Dec IPE futures spread ahead of expiry.
The IPE, Cargill and AIC declined to comment.
